findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher never actually checks the grant shortcut
findings.body: In the new isAccessTokenId matcher, the grant-type check is doubly wrong: (1) the condition is inverted — `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the match when the shortcut EQUALS the expected one, instead of when it does not; (2) the indices are wrong — in a token ID like `onrtac:<uuid>` the grant shortcut occupies character indices 4-5 (`substring(4, 6)`), but `substring(3, 5)` grabs the 2nd char of the token-type shortcut plus the 1st char of the grant shortcut (e.g. "ta" for "onrtac"), which never equals any expected shortcut. Net effect: the matcher accepts any token ID of the form `<anything>:<UUID>` regardless of grant type, so expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken do not actually verify the encoded grant type — the tests pass even if the encoding is wrong. Additionally, if the prefix before ':' is shorter than 5 characters, substring(3, 5) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning a clean non-match.

findings.title: Grant type is only encoded for the standard token-exchange provider, not for legacy/impersonation/federated exchanges
findings.body: The PR's stated motivation includes knowing the grant type for token-exchange use-cases, but `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE)` was only added to StandardTokenExchangeProvider. Other token-exchange implementations that extend AbstractTokenExchangeProvider — the legacy token exchange (V1) provider, subject-impersonation, and federated token exchange — never set this attribute, so access tokens issued through those flows are encoded with the 'na' (unknown) grant shortcut even though they went through the token-exchange grant. Any follow-up logic that relies on the encoded grant type (e.g. #37117) will silently misidentify these tokens.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations at runtime
findings.body: Adding `String getShortcut();` as a new abstract method to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory interface means any existing third-party/custom grant-type factory compiled against the previous interface will throw AbstractMethodError at server startup, because DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()` for every registered OAuth2 grant factory — this aborts postInit and prevents the server from starting. Custom grant types are a documented extension point of this SPI. Providing a default method (e.g. returning a derived or null shortcut that is then handled) would avoid breaking existing deployments on upgrade.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice and never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: In the AccessTokenContext constructor, the second requireNonNull call checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId` (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`). As a result a null rawTokenId is silently accepted despite the message saying otherwise, and encodeTokenId would then produce a token ID ending in `...:null`. The check should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes via a masked NullPointerException, not the intended parse error
findings.body: In the test setup, DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit is never called, so `sessionFactory` is null. When testIncorrectGrantType parses `ofrtac:5678`, the unknown shortcut 'ac' takes the lazy-refresh path in getGrantTypeByShortcut, which calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)` and throws a NullPointerException. The test catches the overly broad `RuntimeException`, so it passes for the wrong reason and would not distinguish a real IllegalArgumentException from the production parse-validation path from an NPE caused by incomplete test setup. The test should either initialize the factory through postInit (or stub the maps so no lazy refresh is needed) and assert on IllegalArgumentException specifically.
